name: TX-29
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+17 district with a sitting Democratic incumbent
Challenger raised about $485 versus Garcia's $1.2 million plus outside support
Prediction markets price Garcia near 97% to win
No public polling, so the margin rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The district's D+17 lean, Garcia's incumbency, and her overwhelming financial edge over a challenger who has raised under $500 all point to an easy Democratic hold, and prediction markets agree at roughly 97 percent for Garcia.
model.watch: A late wave of Republican outside spending or any polling showing a far tighter race would be the main signal that this is becoming competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Texas's 29th District, anchored in Houston, leans Democratic by about seventeen points, and Sylvia Garcia is seeking another term as its incumbent. No public general-election polling tracks this race, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive, so the picture rests on district fundamentals, campaign money, and market pricing. Those all point the same way.

Garcia has raised roughly $1.2 million and benefits from more than $560,000 in outside support, while Republican Martha Fierro has reported only a few hundred dollars in contributions. Prediction markets give Garcia about a 97 percent chance of winning. With a strong incumbent, a heavily Democratic electorate, and a challenger lacking visible resources, Garcia is positioned to win comfortably, though the absence of polling leaves some uncertainty about the exact size of her margin.
